blocks.text: The cult magazine by artist Maurizio Cattelan and photographer Pierpaolo Ferrari makes its return this autumn with Damiani Books, bringing a new issue of images as inventive as they are sharp, and an exhibition in Shenzhen, China.
By Guénola Pellen. Photos by Toiletpaper.

The 21st edition of Toiletpaper opens with a cover that conjures Martin Parr’s grotesque vision of summer leisure and the streak of bad taste that is the magazine’s hallmark. An elderly woman photographed from behind, blue swimsuit, pink plastic bag on her arm: her scarlet back reveals, in negative, a smiley face of unburned skin. Maurizio Cattelan, iconoclastic provocateur of the contemporary art world, and Pierpaolo Ferrari, art director whose practice blends fashion, advertising and surrealism, staged every inch of it.

The editorial venture was born of their first collaboration for W Magazine in 2009. “We had so much fun, we said, why don’t we do more of this?” Maurizio Cattelan told The New Yorker in 2011. Toiletpaper launched the following year: not a word, not an advertisement. Every image is built entirely in camera, meticulously staged tableaux vivants with saturated chromatism that subvert the codes of advertising, fashion and cinema.

“We keep homing in on what a Toiletpaper image is. Like distilling a perfume. It’s not about one particular style or time frame; what makes them Toiletpaper is a special twist. An uncanny ambiguity,” Maurizio Cattelan told The New Yorker in the same interview. In this edition, a monkey wrench locks itself around an ear, a fuchsia stiletto brims with a banana split in an equivocal nod to food porn, and a chef’s knife is held upside down, its bare blade turned toward the very hand that brandishes it: chic, precise and sovereignly unsettling.

Published three years after its predecessor, the issue is accompanied by an exhibition at the Fotografiska museum in Shenzhen, China, and a limited-edition 2027 calendar created with German photographer Ellen von Unwerth, high priestess of fashion and glamour photography.

Toiletpaper Magazine 21 , by Maurizio Cattelan and Pierpaolo Ferrari, is published by Damiani Books , 40 pages, softcover, $20. “ToiletFotoPaperGrafiska” , Toiletpaper’s first exhibition in China, runs from October 1st, 2026 to March 14, 2027 at Fotografiska Shenzhen .
